v2_1_limitation_ledger: v2.1 held 111 cases with exactly ONE never_landed case, and every fully expressible presence value was 'removed'. The cross-implementation test of 2026-08-26 turned on the removed/never_landed distinction and found that the fixture built to test it barely represented it. v2.2 adds six cases in response. This ledger exists so v2.1 is not read retroactively as having tested more than it did.

v2_2_additions.observation_convention_note: All six carry a top-level observed_<date> field. 110 of the 111 v2.1 cases already did; the one exception (registry_update_not_landed) is a must-not-mark case whose observation sits in recorded, so nothing ever had to read it. Authoring the new cases in that exception's style made them undetectable to a consumer that extracts observations from top-level observed_* keys — which is how the reference checker does it. The convention was load-bearing and undocumented; it is documented here.
v2_2_additions.matched_trio: A present, B(i) removal exposed on the discovery surface, B(ii) removal in prose only, C never landed — one convention, four cases. B is split because the split is the finding: B(ii) and C are observationally identical to a consumer reading the machine index, demonstrated on two independently built implementations.
v2_2_additions.intake_pair: acknowledged_then_silent, where a dated acceptance converts later silence from deniable lag into checkable falsity, and its must-not-mark twin acknowledged_registered_late, so a checker cannot score latency as disappearance. Offered on knowledge-catalog#207.
v2_2_additions.new_recorded_key: discovery_surface — where, if anywhere, a surviving absence assertion is machine-readable
v2_2_additions.producer_instances_2026_09_03: On 2026-09-01 the producer (andrewcrenshaw/remember-okf-sample-bundle) shipped the repair the cross-test validated, at 55e6493945a51c77e8a002630dc4890e90d7123e, and tagged the pre-repair state pre-absence-records at ea18185f49948a6832e052a1f0c9c6a935076b95. The matched trio A/B(i)/B(ii)/C now has real producer instances rather than constructed ones: B(ii)'s observed interval is closed, B(i) and C are instantiated on the machine-readable surface. Two further cases record the collision one level up that building the repair surfaced: an empty absences map with the reconciliation key (must-not-mark) and without it (cannot conclude).

v2_2_conformance_note: v2.2 is the first discriminating cut against the current reference implementation: the UNREPAIRED reference consumer fails the fixture; a repaired consumer differing by one absence-record lookup passes it. Reference results, reference_verdict.py: unrepaired — 3 true positives, 2 false positives, must-not-mark FAILED; repaired — 3 true positives, 0 false positives, must-not-mark passed. v2.1 did not contain a case that forced the removed-versus-never-landed distinction at the discovery surface, so the reference consumer could pass without implementing that lookup.
observation_convention_note: The observation convention was load-bearing for the reference verifier and was not explicit in this corpus's schema. 110 of 111 v2.1 cases carry a top-level observed_<date> field; the one exception is a must-not-mark case whose observation sits in recorded.observed_condition, so no tool ever had to read it. Six cases authored in that form during the v2.2 cut were invisible to the verifier until changed. Repaired at schema level rather than noted: deletion-fixture.schema.json now declares observation_convention — canonical location, permitted alternate, and a MUST that conforming tooling normalize both. reference_verdict.py implements the rule.
